ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਆਧਾਰੁ ਜਨ ਕਾ ਆਸਰਾ ॥:
Declares the Divine's lotus feet as the believer's support and refuge, praising them as the life‑anchor for humble servants. The concrete image (lotus feet) stands for shelter and sustenance; dependence on those feet steadies the soul, sustains life, and invites surrender and trust. It functions as exhortation and assurance: make the Divine your support, your shelter, your anchor. (aasra = refuge; bhagat = devotee)

Themes: lotus feet, refuge/anchor, surrender, support of life, devotion (bhakti), trust, shelter, steadying the soul
ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਸੇਵੀ ਰਿਦ ਅੰਤਰਿ ਗੁਰ ਪੂਰੇ ਕੈ ਆਧਾਰਿ:
Commands the seeker to serve the Divine’s lotus feet as an inner practice and to take the Support of the Perfect Guru (spiritual teacher). It instructs heartfelt devotion and surrender, admonishing the mind to fix its attention—to interiorize the image of the feet, to keep that meditation/simran (loving remembrance) in the heart, and to rely on the Guru as refuge and support.

Themes: lotus feet (image of refuge), guru (support, guidance), inner meditation/simran, surrender, devotion, heart-concentration, refuge, reliance
ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਸਿਉ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਿ ਰੀਤਿ ਸੰਤਨ ਮਨਿ ਆਵਏ ਜੀਉ:
Lotus feet (a concrete image of refuge and surrender) stands for wholehearted devotion; this declares that love of the Lord’s lotus feet is the settled code and life-practice of the sant (saints). It affirms an inward disposition: their minds dwell on humble reverence, clinging love, and devoted service to the Divine.

Themes: lotus feet/refuge, love/devotion, sant (saints), inner disposition, way of life, surrender, simran (loving remembrance)
ਬੋਹਿਥੜਾ ਹਰਿ ਚਰਣ ਮਨ ਚੜਿ ਲੰਘੀਐ ॥:
A direct admonition to the mind: the Lord’s lotus feet are pictured as a beautiful boat; climb aboard and be ferried across the ocean of worldly existence. It urges active surrender and refuge — take the Divine feet as your vessel, commit your will, and be carried over maya to liberation. It instructs, commands, and promises safe crossing.

Themes: lotus feet (Divine refuge), boat/boat-of-feet (vehicle), crossing the ocean of maya, surrender/refuge, address to the mind, deliverance/liberation
ਹਰਿ ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਮਨੁ ਬੇਧਿਆ ਕਿਛੁ ਆਨ ਨ ਮੀਠਾ ਰਾਮ:
Lotus feet as a concrete image: the believer’s mind is transfixed and pierced by the Divine presence, signaling total surrender, refuge and single-pointed absorption. The heart finds only the Lord King sweet; all other pleasures and maya (worldly attachment) lose their taste. It praises fixation in naam (the divine Name) and simran (loving remembrance) as the soul’s sole delight.

Themes: lotus feet, surrender/refuge, naam (the divine Name), simran (loving remembrance), renunciation of maya, divine sovereignty, single-pointed devotion
ਪੀ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਆਘਾਨਿਆ ਗੁਰਿ ਅਮਰੁ ਕਰਾਇਆ ॥੨॥:
Drinking the Ambrosial Nectar (naam, the divine Name; simran, loving remembrance) is presented as spiritual consummation: inner thirst quenched, the soul is satisfied and made secure. The Guru’s grace actively grants immortality—removes old age, death and pain. The tone praises and certifies a achieved state: fulfilled contentment, liberation from decay, and release from suffering through divine remembrance and the Guru’s gift.

Themes: Ambrosial Nectar (image of spiritual sustenance; naam/simran), drinking/internalizing divine remembrance, Guru’s grace as bestower of immortality, freedom from old age and death, satisfaction/contentment, end of suffering (mukti)
ਜਿਨ੍ਹ ਪੀਆ ਸੇ ਮਸਤ ਭਏ ਹੈ ਤੂਟੇ ਬੰਧਨ ਫਾਹੇ ॥:
Drinking the naam-ras (the naam, divine Name, as nectar) enraptures and intoxicates the soul; the line praises and declares a causal transformation: those who imbibe the Name are absorbed in divine bliss, and in that spiritual rapture the bonds and shackles of maya (worldly attachment) snap away — release, freedom, inward liberation result.

Themes: naam-ras, drinking/nectar, enrapturement/ecstasy, bonds/shackles broken, maya (worldly attachment), liberation/freedom, simran (loving remembrance)
ਹਰਿ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਸੋ ਚਖੈ ਮੇਰੇ ਮਨਾ ॥੨॥:
Addressing the inner mind, it praises and urges surrender: to "taste the Lord's ambrosial nectar" is a concrete drinking image for imbibing naam (the Divine Name) and simran (loving remembrance) as life-giving spiritual water. It declares that receiving the Naam brings spiritual life, immortal bliss, inner awakening and liberation, and it summons the mind to drink.

Themes: ambrosial nectar, drinking image and nourishment, naam (the Divine Name), simran (loving remembrance), spiritual life, bliss/immortality, inner admonition, liberation
ਹਰਿ ਰਸੁ ਪੀਵਹੁ ਭਾਈ ॥:
An imperative exhortation addressed to siblings: drink the Lord's rasa—take shelter in the Perfect Guru and make the divine Name (naam) your inward draught through constant simran (loving remembrance). It urges surrender, repeated remembrance, and internalizing God’s essence instead of pursuing maya, transforming life into spiritual nourishment.

Themes: drinking the Lord’s rasa, naam (divine Name), simran (loving remembrance), Guru-saran (taking refuge in the Guru), surrender, renunciation of maya, inner transformation
ਗੁਰਿ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਹਰਿ ਮੁਖਿ ਚੋਇਆ ਮੇਰੀ ਜਿੰਦੁੜੀ:
Guru pours ambrosial nectar (amrit) of naam (the divine Name) into the mouth, reviving a spiritually dead person; it addresses the soul, praises the Guru's life-giving grace and declares inner resurrection. Nectar-in-the-mouth images receiving naam and rebirth: the dead self becomes alive, spiritual death transformed into living devotion.

Themes: ambrosial nectar (amrit), naam (the divine Name), mouth as receptacle, Guru's grace, spiritual rebirth, inner resurrection, reception of naam, inner awakening
ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਨਾਮੁ ਨਿਧਾਨੁ ਹੈ ਮਿਲਿ ਪੀਵਹੁ ਭਾਈ ॥:
Praises and urges: Naam (the divine Name) is declared an amrit—ambrosial, life-giving treasure—and the text commands communal reception. It calls siblings to gather in sangat (the company of the devout) and “drink” this nectar together; take refuge in the Name, partake of its immortalizing sweetness, be refreshed and transformed by shared devotion.

Themes: Naam (the divine Name), amrit (ambrosial nectar), sangat (the company of the devout), communal practice, refuge, spiritual treasure, devotion, simran (loving remembrance)
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਭਉ ਕਟਿਓਨੁ ਫਿਰਿ ਜੋਨਿ ਨ ਪਾਏ ॥:
The Divine removed the terror of birth and death from the person, freeing him from being born again; the line declares deliverance by Divine act and offers reassurance and praise. Death's fear vanishes, the soul is released from the cycle of rebirth, and final freedom—mukti (liberation)—is secured so the one is no longer subject to reincarnation.

Themes: fear of birth and death, liberation (mukti), release from rebirth, Divine grace, assurance, deathlessness, emancipation
ਸਹਜੁ ਭਇਆ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਪਾਇਆ ਜਮ ਕਾ ਭਉ ਲਥਾ ॥੨੦॥:
Establishing sahaj (intuitive poise) brings direct union with God and removes the fear of the Messenger of Death; a settled, effortless mind meets the Divine, dissolves terror of mortality, and makes spiritual death unable to touch the soul. The line proclaims attainment and reassures seekers—praising inner calm, declaring freedom from death’s dread, and instructing the mind toward steady, natural balance.

Themes: sahaj (intuitive poise), union with God, fearlessness, Messenger of Death (death as image), steadiness of mind, liberation, reassurance, instruction to the seeker
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਭਉ ਕਟੀਐ ਜਨ ਕਾ ਸਬਦੁ ਜਪਿ ॥:
Offers freedom from the fear of birth and death by immersing the mind in the shabad (Divine Word) of the sevak (humble servant). In sadh sangat (the company of the devout), reading and simran (loving remembrance) of that praise-bani cuts away the dread of rebirth, removes mortality-anxiety, and brings calm, release and spiritual safety.

Themes: birth and death (samsara), shabad (Divine Word), sevak’s praise-bani, sadh sangat (company of the devout), simran (loving remembrance), dispelling fear, liberation
ਨ ਦਨੋਤਿ ਜਸਮਰਣੇਨ ਜਨਮ ਜਰਾਧਿ ਮਰਣ ਭਇਅੰ ॥੧॥ ਰ:
Calling the mind to simran (loving remembrance) in meditation, the speaker instructs and reassures: sustained remembrance of the Divine removes the dread of birth, old age, worry and death. Meditative focus dissolves fear of rebirth and mortality; practicing simran ends anxiety about aging and dying and promises liberation from the cycle of birth-and-death.

Themes: simran (loving remembrance), freedom from fear, birth and death, aging and worry, liberation from samsara, instruction/assurance
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਦੁਖੁ ਕਾਟੀਐ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਚੂਕੈ ਜਮ ਕੀ ਕਾਣੇ:
Declares a promise of liberation: the pains of birth and death are cut away and the terror of Yama, the Messenger of Death, is ended. It assures and exhorts—seek refuge in the company of the devout (sangat) so lifelong suffering is removed; freedom from cyclic birth–death and the fear of dying is declared and offered. Translation/teeka conflict: translation addresses the Beloved, teeka reads it as exhorting the listener to join sangat.

Themes: birth–death suffering, liberation/moksha, fear of Yama (death), sangat (company of the devout), refuge and surrender, assurance/promise, cutting worldly bondage (maya)
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਭੈ ਲਾਥੇ ॥੪॥੨॥੫੨॥:
Declares a personal release from the image of birth and death: the speaker’s fear of being born again or of dying is ended. Proclaims a settled, fearless state after spiritual realization—fear of rebirth and mortality erased, anxiety about the cycle of existence removed. Presents liberation as accomplished fact, comforting and steadying the mind with serene detachment from worldly clinging.

Themes: birth-and-death (cycle of rebirth), fearlessness, liberation, release from samsara, inner peace, detachment, assurance, testimony
ਸਾਧਸੰਗਤਿ ਕੈ ਆਸਰੈ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਸਿਉ ਰੰਗੁ ਲਾਏ ॥:
The Saadh Sangat (the Company of the Holy) is named as refuge and support; by dwelling in that sacred company the seeker is drawn into love of God. The line praises and instructs: take shelter in congregational devotion, rely on holy companionship to turn the heart toward the Divine, to become enamored, attached, and surrendered to God.

Themes: Saadh Sangat (holy company), refuge/support, divine love, devotion, surrender, spiritual companionship, attachment to God, simran (remembrance)
ਸਾਧੂ ਸੰਗਿ ਤਰੀਜੈ ਸਾਗਰੁ ਕਟੀਐ ਜਮ ਕੀ ਫਾਸਾ ਜੀ:
Commands the seeker to take refuge in the Saadh Sangat: join the holy company (sangat, the company of the devout) to cross the world-ocean and be saved. Instructive and assuring, it urges communal devotion as the means to transcend samsaric waters, to pass beyond worldly suffering, and to have the noose of death cut away — freedom from death and rebirth.

Themes: sangat (the company of the devout), refuge and surrender, crossing the world-ocean, liberation from death and rebirth, cutting the noose of death, communal devotion, transcendence
ਸਾਧਸੰਗਤਿ ਕੀ ਭੀਰ ਜਉ ਪਾਈ ਤਉ ਨਾਨਕ ਹਰਿ ਸੰਗਿ:
Joining the Saadh Sangat (company of the holy) brought the poet into direct meeting with Har (the Lord). It praises and testifies: holy fellowship is the concrete means to divine encounter, opening the heart to union, making God present in company, and endorsing seeking that community as the path to realize God. Translation and teeka agree.

Themes: Saadh Sangat (company of the holy), Har (the Lord), divine union/meeting, spiritual fellowship, testimony/praise, seeking community, inner transformation
ਸੰਤਤ ਹੀ ਸਤਸੰਗਤਿ ਸੰਗ ਸੁਰੰਗ ਰਤੇ ਜਸੁ ਗਾਵਤ ਹ:
Saints abide perpetually in the saadh sangat (the Company of the Holy), soaked in one sweet spiritual taste and dyed in a lovely hue of divine love, and they continuously sing the Lord’s praises. The passage praises that steady, communal immersion, honors their unbroken devotional mood, and points the reader to emulate constant fellowship, single-hearted devotion, and ceaseless praise.

Themes: saadh sangat (Company of the Holy), constant immersion, single rasa (one sweet spiritual taste), devotional singing, divine love, communal worship, emulate the saints.
ਕਾਢਿ ਲੀਏ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਆਨ ਬਿਖੈ ਤੇ ਸਾਧਸੰਗਿ ਮਨੁ ਲਾਵ:
A pleading petition asking God to lift the speaker out of vice and corruption—an image of divine extraction—and to attach the mind to Saadh Sangat (the Company of the Holy). It seeks rescue and reorientation: remove worldly entanglement, extract pride/poison, and fix the heart in holy company; surrendering agency to divine placement rather than self-will.

Themes: petitionary prayer, divine rescue, Saadh Sangat (Company of the Holy), removal of maya (worldly attachment), reorientation of mind, surrender, purification
ਮਹਿਮਾ ਸਾਧੂ ਸੰਗ ਕੀ ਸੁਨਹੁ ਮੇਰੇ ਮੀਤਾ ॥:
Praises the glory of the saadh sangat (company of the holy) and urges attentive hearing; it exalts the Guru's sangat as a living source of sanctity, refuge and spiritual power, calling friends to lean in and receive its benefit. The holy fellowship is celebrated, its greatness proclaimed, and the listener is commanded to listen closely and accept its transforming presence.

Themes: saadh sangat (company of the holy), Guru's sangat (Guru's company), praise/exaltation, attentive listening, refuge and transformation, simran (loving remembrance)
ਮੇਰਾ ਗੁਰੁ ਪਰਮੇਸਰੁ ਸੁਖਦਾਈ ॥:
Names the Guru as Parmesar (Transcendent Lord) and as the source of all comfort and peace; it praises and proclaims the teacher as literally God, collapsing guide and Divine into one presence. The statement functions as assurance and refuge: trust and surrender to the Guru yield spiritual and worldly peace, the dispenser of solace and lasting tranquility—repeated as giver of peace, source of all sukhdai.

Themes: Guru (teacher as Divine), Parmesar (Transcendent Lord), refuge and surrender, peace (sukhdai), assurance, devotion, divine identity, grace
ਤੁਮ ਦਾਤੇ ਤੁਮ ਪੁਰਖ ਬਿਧਾਤੇ ॥:
Declares God as the universal Giver and the Architect of destiny: the Creator who brings all beings into being, pervades everything, and dispenses gifts and fortunes. Praising divine sovereignty and providence, it asserts human dependence on the Lord’s will, urges trust and surrender, and frames every blessing and life-course as granted and arranged by the Divine.

Themes: divine giver, creator, ordainer of destiny, providence, divine pervasiveness, trust and surrender, human dependence
ਕਰੁਣਾ ਮੈ ਕਿਰਪਾਲ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾ ਨਿਧਿ ਜੀਵਨ ਪਦ ਨਾਨਕ:
Praises the Divine as embodiment of kindness and a treasure of compassion (kirpa), while pleading for darshan (vision of the Divine) that grants an uplifted, redeemed human life; declares that beholding God’s presence bestows spiritual elevation, liberation-in-life, and the rank of true living. The teeka reads this as a direct petition—“give me Your darshan”—not only a statement of attainment.

Themes: compassion (kirpa), darshan (vision of the Divine), praise and plea, spiritual uplift, redemption in life, grace, devotion
ਤੂੰ ਭਾਰੋ ਠਾਕੁਰੁ ਗੁਣੀ ਗਹੇਰਾ ॥੨॥:
Declares the Divine as a personal Sovereign and Master—an intimate "my Lord and Master"—and praises God as a treasure chest of excellence, full of virtues. It affirms God's overflowing goodness and deep-hearted compassion (teeka: filled with all virtues, profound in soul), offering refuge and demanding surrender and trust. Restated: sovereign ruler, abundant store of virtue, profound compassionate source.

Themes: praise, sovereignty/mastery, virtues-as-treasure, inner depth/compassion, refuge/surrender, devotion/trust
ਦੇਵਣਹਾਰੁ ਦਾਤਾਰੁ ਕਿਤੁ ਮੁਖਿ ਸਾਲਾਹੀਐ ॥:
Proclaims the Lord as the all-giving Sustainer—the Great Giver and generous Donor who supplies rizq (provision) to every being—and immediately confesses human inability to praise Him adequately: with what mouth can one extol such bounty? It exalts Divine generosity while admitting words, names (naam) and speech fail, cultivating humble awe and grateful surrender.

Themes: Divine generosity (Great Giver), sustenance (rizq), mouth/praise and speech's failure, humility before God, gratitude and awe, praise versus silence
ਤੇਰੇ ਕਵਨ ਕਵਨ ਗੁਣ ਕਹਿ ਕਹਿ ਗਾਵਾ ਤੂ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਗ:
Addressing God as sahib (Lord/Master), the speaker marvels that no single attribute can be fully praised: which of Your countless virtues should I sing? Calling God the owner, sustainer and the treasure of excellence, the voice pours out adoration, admits human incapacity to enumerate divine perfections, and surrenders in awe before divine sovereignty and endless worth.

Themes: treasure of virtues (image and idea), sahib/sovereignty, praise and wonder, inability to enumerate, humility before God, surrender/devotion, sustainer/keeper
ਰੇ ਬਉਰੇ ਤੁਹਿ ਘਰੀ ਨ ਰਾਖੈ ਕੋਈ ॥:
Addressing the "mad-man" with an affectionate rebuke, it warns that no one will let you stay in their home even for a moment — the concrete image of being denied shelter. It scolds the mind, admonishing against expecting others' protection or permanence; you will be abandoned, refused, left without support.

Themes: abandonment, impermanence, admonition to the mind, social rejection, home/shelter image, maya (worldly attachment), affectionate rebuke
ਕਾਹੇ ਮਨ ਤੂ ਡੋਲਤਾ ਹਰਿ ਮਨਸਾ ਪੂਰਣਹਾਰੁ ॥:
Admonishing the wavering inner self: the mind is rebuked for oscillating and told to cease doubting, because the Lord is the fulfiller of hopes and desires. It commands steady trust and surrender, urging loving remembrance (simran) and fixation on the Naam (the divine Name). Stop mental vacillation; be steadfast in faith; God completes longings and satisfies wishes, bringing peace.

Themes: wavering mind, steadfast trust in God, God as fulfiller of desires, surrender, simran (loving remembrance), naam (the divine Name), faith, inner peace
ਰੇ ਮਨ ਤੂ ਭੀ ਭਜੁ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ॥੨॥:
Addresses the inner self—“O my mind”—and commands it to do bhajan: to meditate, repeat and vibrate the divine Name (naam) of the Lord of the Universe. It admonishes and instructs the mind into simran (loving remembrance), urging steady, vocal or silent repetition, inward turning and disciplined devotion so the inner attention becomes constant praise and surrender.

Themes: mind (inner self), naam (divine Name) / simran, bhajan (meditation & vibration), command/admonition, devotion, disciplined practice, Lord of the Universe
ਮਨ ਮੇਰਿਆ ਅੰਤਰਿ ਤੇਰੈ ਨਿਧਾਨੁ ਹੈ ਬਾਹਰਿ ਵਸਤੁ:
Addressing the mind, this is an admonition and instruction: the concrete image of a hidden treasure names God dwelling within your inner self; stop seeking blessedness outwards in forests, possessions or people. Turn inward, cease external searching, and access spiritual wealth by inward remembrance—simran (loving remembrance) or naam (the divine Name)—rather than chasing maya (worldly attachment).

Themes: inner treasure, admonishing the mind, inward turning, divine immanence, stop external search, simran/naam, renunciation of maya
ਸੁਣਿ ਬਾਵਰੇ ਤੂ ਕਾਏ ਦੇਖਿ ਭੁਲਾਨਾ ॥:
A sharp admonition that wakes the bewildered mind: calling the person "madman" for staring at the world, it scolds and demands attention. The concrete image of gazing at the world exposes fixation on maya (worldly attachment) and labels that fixation spiritual insanity, urging an immediate about-face from the lost life-path and a return to clear, disciplined focus.

Themes: maya (worldly attachment), admonition, heed/listen, spiritual madness, mind’s distraction, return to the path, simran (loving remembrance)
ਸੁਣਿ ਬਾਵਰੇ ਥੀਉ ਰੇਣੁ ਜਿਨੀ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਧਿਆਇਆ ॥:
Addressing the deluded "madman," this is a sharp admonition to adopt utter humility: become the dust beneath the feet of those who do simran (loving remembrance of God). Serve and abase yourself before sincere meditators; surrender ego and cling to their company (sangat) — proximity to the devout is presented as the practical way to attain union with the Divine.

Themes: dust-under-feet (image), humility/surrender, simran (loving remembrance), sangat (the company of the devout), ego-renunciation, service/devotion, path to divine union
ਲਖ ਖੁਸੀਆ ਪਾਤਿਸਾਹੀਆ ਜੇ ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਨਦਰਿ ਕਰੇਇ:
If my satguru (True Guru) bestows nadar (a merciful Glance of Grace) on me, that single look is worth hundreds of thousands of princely pleasures. One merciful glance equals infinite spiritual wealth, replaces all worldly riches, and yields complete contentment; the Guru’s mercy is praised as the supreme, sufficient treasure that dispels attachment to maya.

Themes: satguru, nadar, spiritual wealth, princely pleasures, contentment, renunciation of maya
ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਹੋਇ ਦਇਆਲੁ ਤਾ ਦੁਖੁ ਨ ਜਾਣੀਐ ॥:
The True Guru's mercy (compassionate grace) changes the disciple's inner perception so that blows, loss and pain are not registered as suffering; the heart does not call them sorrow or feel them as hurt. This is an assuring promise and practical instruction: rely on the Guru's compassion to dissolve affliction, produce equanimity, and stop labeling events as pain.

Themes: True Guru, mercy/grace, transformed perception, non-suffering, equanimity, surrender, reframing affliction
ਹਰਿ ਚਉਥੜੀ ਲਾਵ ਮਨਿ ਸਹਜੁ ਭਇਆ ਹਰਿ ਪਾਇਆ ਬਲਿ:
Addresses the Lord in a marriage image: at the fourth circumambulation of the wedding ritual the speaker declares inner calm and spiritual union. It praises and thanks, asserting that by God's grace the mind becomes sahaj (natural, effortless peace) and finds the Lord. It proclaims consummation with the Divine, surrendering oneself in devotion, and describes the resulting unshakable steadiness of heart.

Themes: fourth round (marriage circumambulation; sacred union), sahaj (natural, effortless peace), union with the Lord (spiritual consummation), surrender/devotion (sacrifice to the Lord), divine grace (God’s mercy enabling steadiness), inner steadfastness (unchanging, settled mind)
ਸੁਖੁ ਪਾਇਆ ਸਤਿਗੁਰੂ ਮਨਾਇ ॥:
Pleasing the satguru (True Guru) and enshrining the Guru in the heart grants inner peace and the fulfillment of all desires; the statement declares attainment, not a plea. It praises inward surrender and devotion, saying that cherishing the Guru within brings tranquility, spiritual fruit, and complete contentment. Peace is the outcome of making the Guru one’s refuge and indwelling presence.

Themes: satguru (True Guru), Guru in the heart, inner peace, fulfillment/spiritual fruit, surrender/refuge, simran (loving remembrance), inward transformation
ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਮੇਰਾ ਸਦਾ ਸਹਾਈ ਜਿਨਿ ਦੁਖ ਕਾ ਕਾਟਿਆ:
Declares the True Guru (spiritual teacher) as constant help and refuge, a praised protector in whom one can trust. Portrays the Guru tearing down the banner of pain and cutting the root of suffering — an image of uprooting sorrow and a claim of radical relief. Restates the core three ways: perpetual support, annihilation of suffering’s root, and secure refuge in the Guru.

Themes: True Guru (spiritual teacher), refuge and perpetual help, tearing down the banner of pain, cutting the root of suffering, praise and trust, liberation from affliction
ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਮਿਲਣ ਕੀ ਇਹ ਤੇਰੀ ਬਰੀਆ ॥:
Declares an urgent, singular chance to meet Gobind (the Lord of the Universe) and urges the seeker to seize this moment for divine union. It presses the mind to turn now toward Parmatma, framing access to God as rare and immediate, restating the call as meeting, encounter, and final purpose of human life.

Themes: meeting the Lord (Gobind/Parmatma), rare opportunity/once-only chance, urgency/impermanence, divine union, surrender/refocusing the mind, human life-purpose, simran (loving remembrance)
ਪ੍ਰਾਣੀ ਤੂੰ ਆਇਆ ਲਾਹਾ ਲੈਣਿ ॥:
Addressing the human, it declares that the purpose of birth is to earn spiritual profit — to gain the fruit of naam (the Divine Name). It admonishes and instructs: reorient life toward harvesting naam's benefit, not transient worldly gain, urging inward labour and loving remembrance (simran) to secure the soul’s true profit.

Themes: purpose of life, spiritual profit, naam (the Divine Name), simran (remembrance), admonition, renunciation of maya, inward discipline
ਹਰਿ ਭਗਤਿ ਦ੍ਰਿੜੁ ਮਿਲੁ ਸਾਧ ਨਾਨਕ ਤੇਰੈ ਕਾਮਿ:
Urges a seeker to meet the Holy—seek the saintly Guru or holy company—and to plant devotional worship (bhagati) firmly in the heart. It instructs and admonishes: internalize devotion, root the divine Name (naam) and loving remembrance (simran) within, since only this inner, fixed devotion will avail; nothing else will serve you at the end.

Themes: meeting the Holy (Guru/sangat), bhagati (devotional worship) implanted in the heart, naam/simran, inward transformation, single-pointed practice, practical soteriology, admonition/instruction
ਜੀਵਨਾ ਸਫਲ ਜੀਵਨ ਸੁਨਿ ਹਰਿ ਜਪਿ ਜਪਿ ਸਦ ਜੀਵਨਾ:
Declares that true, successful life is gained by first hearing the divine Name (naam), then continually chanting (jap) and lovingly remembering (simran) it; it praises that discipline and promises abiding, spiritual life. It defines the standard for a fulfilled human life: attentive hearing leads to continual remembrance and chanting, and that sustained devotion transforms mortal existence into everlasting life.

Themes: naam (the divine Name), hearing/listening, chanting (jap), simran (loving remembrance), fruitful life, spiritual immortality, constant practice, devotion
ਸੰਤ ਜਨਾ ਕੀ ਰੇਣੁਕਾ ਲੈ ਮਾਥੈ ਲਾਵਉ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ:
Taking the dust of the Saints’ feet and marking the forehead is praised as the supreme treasure and an act of total surrender; the teeka even equates it to nine treasures and eighteen perfections. It praises and instructs: revere the Saints’ blessing, make that dust your true wealth, humble yourself, and internalize their virtue for simran (loving remembrance).

Themes: dust of the feet (humble relic), forehead anointing (consecration), saints' grace as treasure, surrender, humility, simran (loving remembrance), sangat (company of the devout)
ਗੁਰਸਿਖਾਂ ਕੀ ਹਰਿ ਧੂੜਿ ਦੇਹਿ ਹਮ ਪਾਪੀ ਭੀ ਗਤਿ:
A pleading to be given the dust of the Guru's Sikhs (gursikhs, disciple‑devotees) — the concrete image of holy contact — as a saving blessing. It seeks humble surrender and refuge in devotees' feet, solicits their sanctifying grace and forgiveness, and asks that even a confessed sinner be lifted, cleansed and transformed into an elevated spiritual state.

Themes: humility, surrender, holy contact, grace, transformation, refuge, forgiveness
ਕਰਉ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਭਗਤ ਜਨ ਧੂਰਿ ਮੁਖਿ ਲਾਵਉ ॥੩॥:
Bows in reverence to humble devotees and smears the dust of their feet on the face as a bodily sign of utter humility, surrender and worship. Praises these holy ones and pleads to join their sangat (company of the devout) to practice naam (the divine Name) and bhakti (devotion), longing to emulate them and sing God’s virtues alongside them.

Themes: humility, reverence for saints, longing for sangat, surrender (dust of feet), devotional aspiration, emulation, ardas (prayer/plea)
ਟਹਲ ਕਰਉ ਤੇਰੇ ਦਾਸ ਕੀ ਪਗ ਝਾਰਉ ਬਾਲ ॥:
A plea to be allowed continual, self‑abasing service: literally wiping the devotee’s feet with one’s hair as the image of utter humility. The speaker asks to keep serving God’s servant, turning care of the human devotee into service of the Divine, a vow of ongoing seva (selfless service), reverent surrender and abasement rather than pride.

Themes: wiping feet with hair (utter humility), seva (selfless service), servant-as-path-to-God, pleading for continuity, reverence, surrender, abnegation
ਕਰਿ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਧੂਰਿ ਦੇਹੁ ਸੰਤਨ ਕੀ ਸੁਖੁ ਨਾਨਕੁ ਇ:
The speaker pleads for kirpa (grace): ask God to grant the dust of the sant (saints) — the concrete image of humble proximity, surrender and sanctified contact. He requests divine mercy to give the blessing of saintly association (sangat), access to their feet as refuge through humble service, and thereby secure inner sukh (peace). It is a yearning petition for peace via closeness to the holy.

Themes: grace, saints’ feet (humble refuge), saintly company (sangat), surrender, humble service (seva), yearning, inner peace (sukh)
ਸੰਤਹ ਚਰਣ ਹਮਾਰੋ ਮਾਥਾ ਨੈਨ ਦਰਸੁ ਤਨਿ ਧੂਰਿ ਪਰ:
A pleading petition to remain forever at the saints' feet: to press the forehead on the charan (feet) of the sant (the spiritually realized), to keep the eyes fixed on their darshan (blessed vision), and to let the body be covered with the dust of their feet. It demands humble surrender, constant proximity and service to holy presence, and urgent devotional longing for blessing and guidance.

Themes: sant's feet (refuge, surrender), forehead-on-feet (prostration), darshan (blessed vision), dust of the feet (service and humility), devotional longing, continual presence with the holy, seeking blessing/mercy
ਅਤਿ ਸੁੰਦਰ ਮਨਮੋਹਨ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਸਭਹੂ ਮਧਿ ਨਿਰਾਰੇ ॥:
Addresses the Divine as supremely beautiful Enticer, Beloved — an image of irresistible spiritual attraction and the heart’s refuge. Declares God present in and among all things yet distinct and beyond them: within everything, among everything, and apart from everything. The tone is life-giving praise; these words revive the soul and call to simran (loving remembrance) and naam (the divine Name).

Themes: Divine beauty/Enticer, immanence and transcendence, praise as soul‑giving, refuge and surrender, simran/naam, spiritual revitalization
ਤੇਰਾ ਨਾਮੁ ਰੂੜੋ ਰੂਪੁ ਰੂੜੋ ਅਤਿ ਰੰਗ ਰੂੜੋ ਮੇ:
Addressing "my Lord," the speaker exults in three images: Your naam (the divine Name) is lovely, Your roop (form/appearance) is lovely, and Your rang (hue, the felt color of love) is exceedingly lovely. The line functions as ecstatic praise and surrender — full-throated adoration, savoring divine beauty, repeatedly declaring the heart captivated by Name, form, and the taste of love.

Themes: divine beauty, naam (the divine Name), roop (divine form), rang (the hue of love), ecstatic praise, surrender/devotion, heart's delight
ਸੁੰਦਰ ਰਸਾਲ ਤੂ ॥੧॥:
Declares and praises the Divine as beautiful and the primal source of all nectar (ras). Presents God as the wellspring of spiritual flavors and bliss — the soma (divine ambrosia) from which every sweetness of love, joy, and devotion flows. Exalts God’s attractiveness while naming God the origin, sustainer, and savor of the soul’s delight.

Themes: beauty, nectar (ras), soma (divine ambrosia), source of spiritual bliss, praise, divine attractiveness, origin of all flavors, devotion
ਨੈਣ ਪਸੰਦੋ ਸੋਇ ਪੇਖਿ ਮੁਸਤਾਕ ਭਈ ॥:
The speaker praises the Beloved’s visible beauty as utterly irresistible; the eyes’ gaze of the Divine arrests the mind and produces spiritual intoxication. Beholding the Lord delights and bewitches—sight captivates, the heart is swept away, consciousness is lost in rapture; visual encounter becomes devotional trance and complete absorption in the Beloved.

Themes: eyes/gaze, divine beauty, rapture/intoxication, devotion, surrender, enchantment
ਸੁੰਦਰ ਸੋਭਾ ਲਾਲ ਗੋਪਾਲ ਦਇਆਲ ਕੀ ਅਪਰ ਅਪਾਰਾ ਰ:
Praising the Merciful Lord's radiant beauty and declaring His glory to be everywhere and without limit. Image: the beautiful splendour of Gopaal (Beloved, protector) spread throughout the house of mercy; idea: God's merciful presence fills, adorns and pervades creation. His majesty is resplendent, vast, boundless—beautiful, infinite, without end.

Themes: mercy, divine beauty, boundlessness/infinity, presence, praise, refuge, adornment
ਅਪੁਨੇ ਸੇਵਕ ਕੀ ਆਪੇ ਰਾਖੈ ਆਪੇ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਾਵੈ ॥:
God Himself preserves and honours His servants, sheltering and keeping them safe; He Himself causes them to chant His Name (naam - the divine Name), awakening and sustaining loving remembrance (simran). The declaration reassures and praises divine agency and grace: protection, salvation and the very gift of devotion are granted by the Lord, not produced solely by human effort.

Themes: divine preservation, gift of devotion, naam (divine Name), simran (loving remembrance), grace, protection, surrender
ਭਗਤ ਜਨਾ ਕੀ ਹਰਿ ਜੀਉ ਰਾਖੈ ਜੁਗਿ ਜੁਗਿ ਰਖਦਾ ਆ:
Declares that the Lord protects and upholds His humble bhagat (devotees), preserving their honour and safety; it praises and reassures the faithful, asserting Divine guardianship that endures through every age. Repeats the promise as protection, as preservation of respect, and as an eternal, continuous refuge and care for the devoted.

Themes: divine protection, bhagat (devotees) safety, preservation of honour, eternal constancy, refuge/shelter, assurance/grace
ਭਗਤ ਤੇਰੇ ਸਭਿ ਪ੍ਰਾਣਪਤਿ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਮ ਤੂੰ ਭਗਤਨ ਕਾ:
Addresses God as the owner and beloved of life, calling the Divine both master-sustainer and intimate lover; declares reciprocal affection: bhagat (devotees) are dear to God, and God is dear to the bhagat. Praising and reassuring, it affirms mutual love, refuge in the Divine, and the security of surrender to that beloved Lord.

Themes: beloved, owner-of-life, mutual love, bhakti (devotion), surrender, grace, refuge, praise
ਭਗਤਾ ਕੀ ਟੇਕ ਤੂੰ ਸੰਤਾ ਕੀ ਓਟ ਤੂੰ ਸਚਾ ਸਿਰਜਨ:
Calling the eternal Creator the constant Support and the Saints' Shelter, it praises and reassures the faithful: God — and God’s naam (the divine Name) — is the unfailing prop for bhagat (devotees) and sant (saints). It declares divine protection and refuge, urges trust and surrender, affirms that the Divine presence and Name provide safety, steadiness and solace.

Themes: support, shelter, refuge, naam (divine Name), bhagat (devotee), sant (saint), surrender, divine steadiness
ਹਰਿ ਜੁਗੁ ਜੁਗੁ ਭਗਤ ਉਪਾਇਆ ਪੈਜ ਰਖਦਾ ਆਇਆ ਰਾਮ:
Declares and praises God's steady providence: in every age He brings forth bhagats (devotees) and keeps their standing and respect; He raises spiritual seekers generation after generation and preserves their honor and protection even amid crowds and turmoil. The statement comforts and assures the faithful by asserting the Lord King's continual creation, safeguarding, and public upholding of devotees' dignity.

Themes: creating devotees (birthing spiritual seekers), preserving honor (upholding dignity and reputation), Lord as sovereign (Lord King), continuity across ages, divine providence, assurance/comfort, protection amid crowds
ਹਮਰੇ ਕਰਮ ਨ ਬਿਚਰਹੁ ਠਾਕੁਰ ਤੁਮ੍ਹ ਪੈਜ ਰਖਹੁ ਅ:
A pleading address to the Thakur (Lord/Master): do not count or judge my karma (actions/consequences), and keep the honor and standing of Your sevak (servant/devotee) intact. The speaker refuses karmic accounting and instead seeks the Master's protection and preservation of reputation; asking for mercy and shelter rather than legal judgment, surrendering to Divine grace and refuge.

Themes: mercy, divine grace, karma (actions/consequences), refuge in the Master, servant’s honor, pleading, surrender
ਜਾਚਿਕੁ ਮੰਗੈ ਨਿਤ ਨਾਮੁ ਸਾਹਿਬੁ ਕਰੇ ਕਬੂਲੁ ॥:
Paints the seeker as a humble beggar who asks every day for the Lord’s Name: if one persistently begs for naam (the divine Name) and keeps loving simran (remembrance), the Lord and Master accepts and grants the petition. It is instructing and promising — daily, humble pleading for naam secures divine acceptance; persistent asking wins God’s grace.

Themes: beggar image, naam (divine Name), simran (remembrance), humility, persistence, divine acceptance, grace
ਦੇਹਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਸੰਤੋਖੀਆ ਉਤਰੈ ਮਨ ਕੀ ਭੁਖ ॥:
A direct pleading for divine gift: give me Your naam (the divine Name) so santokh (contentment) comes and the hunger of my mind is satisfied. The concrete image is receiving the Name; the underlying claim is that God's Name, when bestowed and held in the heart, quenches craving, ends mental thirst, removes longing, and makes the heart calm, fulfilled and sufficient.

Themes: petition, naam (divine Name), santokh (contentment), inner hunger/craving, divine grace, fulfillment, cessation of desire
ਜਾਚਿਕੁ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਾਚੈ ਜਾਚੈ ॥:
Humble beggar image: the speaker repeatedly begs for naam (the Divine Name), pleading to God as refuge, owner, and giver of all comforts. The double pleading shows urgent, continuous simran (loving remembrance), single‑minded longing, radical dependence and humble surrender, seeking sustenance and rescue solely in the Name.

Themes: begging, naam, dependence, simran, humility, refuge
ਕਰਹੁ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾ ਗੋਪਾਲ ਗੋਬਿਦੇ ਅਪਨਾ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਾਵਹ:
An urgent plea for kripa (mercy): addressing God as Gopal/Gobind — both nurturing caretaker and sovereign Lord — the devotee begs to be enabled to japa the Naam (chant the divine Name). It confesses human incapacity and asks for grace and help to keep simran (loving remembrance), surrendering personal effort to God’s sustaining power.

Themes: mercy, divine names as sustainer and sovereign, petitionary prayer, grace enabling simran, dependence on God, devotion
ਜਾਚਕੁ ਮੰਗੈ ਦਾਨੁ ਦੇਹਿ ਪਿਆਰਿਆ ॥:
The speaker adopts the concrete image of a beggar, pleading for daan (charity) from the Beloved — a request not for worldly alms but for the khaer (welfare) of the boundless Shabad (Divine Word). It functions as a direct, humble petition for divine mercy and the gift of naam (the Divine Name), modeling surrender and dependence and urging devotees to ask for spiritual blessing rather than worldly gain. The teeka clarifies the charity sought is the benefit of the eternal Word.

Themes: beggar image, daan (charity) as spiritual gift, petition/pleading, Beloved (Divine), Shabad (Divine Word), naam (Divine Name), humility, surrender.
ਦਰਿ ਮੰਗਤੁ ਜਾਚੈ ਦਾਨੁ ਹਰਿ ਦੀਜੈ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾ ਕਰਿ:
A humble supplicant stands at the Lord’s Door as a beggar, pleading for dan (charity) and kripa (mercy); the image is literal begging and also a confession of total dependence on divine grace. The speaker begs for compassionate giving, beseeches God’s favor, and asks for spiritual bounty rather than claiming merit. The stance is urgent pleading, surrender, and seeking transformative mercy.

Themes: supplication, humility, divine mercy (kripa), charity/grace (dan), surrender, dependence on God, spiritual poverty
ਮਉਲਿਓ ਮਨੁ ਤਨੁ ਹੋਇਓ ਹਰਿਆ ਏਕ ਬੂੰਦ ਜਿਨਿ ਪਾਈ:
One small drop of naam-jal (spiritual water of the Name) floods the whole inner life: the mind blossoms, the body greenly revives, and the soul awakens. A single taste of the Name quickens the heart, enlivens the frame, opens receptivity, and declares that a tiny portion of divine nectar effects total spiritual flowering and flourishing.

Themes: single drop, naam (the divine Name), naam-jal (spiritual water), spiritual flowering, inner transformation, revitalized body, grace, simran (loving remembrance)
ਹਰਿ ਰਸੁ ਪੀਵਤ ਸਦ ਹੀ ਰਾਤਾ ॥:
A concrete image of drinking the Lord’s nectar: one who drinks naam (the divine Name), the naam-amrit, becomes forever dyed in that taste. Declaring and praising a permanent inner transformation: imbibing the Divine soaks and saturates the mind, colors the heart, and leaves the person continually steeped in divine remembrance and abiding union.

Themes: drinking nectar, naam (the divine Name), naam-amrit, lasting transformation, immersion, naam-rang (being coloured by the Name), abiding union
ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਰਸੁ ਕੀਰਤਨੁ ਹਰਿ ਗਾਈਐ ਅਹਿਨਿਸਿ ਪੂਰਨ:
Declare the Lord's kirtan (devotional singing) as amrit ras (life-giving ambrosial essence) and command the mind to sing it without ceasing. The line exhorts continuous kirtan, promising that the pooran naad (full Sound-current) will vibrate day and night, producing inner music, constant spiritual vitality and unceasing bliss.

Themes: amrit ras (ambrosial nectar), kirtan (devotional singing), naad (primordial Sound-current), continuous practice, inner resonance, spiritual life, bliss, exhortation
ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਰਸਨਾ ਪੀਉ ਪਿਆਰੀ ॥:
An affectionate command to the beloved tongue to drink the ambrosial nectar (amrit) of naam (the divine Name). It urges the faculty of speech and taste to internalize and savor Naam-rasa, to engage in simran (loving remembrance) and recitation; a sensory discipline that feeds and enlivens the soul, giving spiritual life and displacing worldly tastes.

Themes: tongue (jeebh), ambrosial nectar (amrit), naam (the divine Name), naam-rasa (divine taste), simran (loving remembrance), sensory discipline, spiritual nourishment, life-giving practice
ਤੇਰਾ ਜਨੁ ਰਾਮ ਰਸਾਇਣਿ ਮਾਤਾ ॥:
A humble servant declares ecstatic intoxication in the Divine ambrosial essence, praising God by reporting total absorption and surrender. The concrete image of tasting/drinking the rasa (nectar) says the soul is enraptured, lost in bliss, drunk on naam (the divine Name); the stance is testimonial and exemplary, modelling the ideal state achieved through loving remembrance (simran).

Themes: devotion, intoxication/rapture, naam (the divine Name), nectar/taste, surrender/humility, simran (loving remembrance), absorption, exemplar of bhakti.
ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਰਸੁ ਪੀਆ ਗੁਰ ਸਬਦੀ ਹਮ ਨਾਮ ਵਿਟਹੁ ਕ:
Declares that by drinking the Ambrosial Essence (amrit) of naam (the divine Name) through the Guru's Shabad (Word), the speaker receives spiritual life and lays down the self as a sacrifice to Naam. Praises the Shabad's life-giving power, restates that naam becomes inner nectar, and models total surrender and devotional offering.

Themes: Guru's Shabad (Word), naam (the divine Name), amrit/ambrosial nectar, spiritual nourishment, surrender, sacrifice, devotion
ਰਸੁ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਨਾਮੁ ਰਸੁ ਅਤਿ ਭਲਾ ਕਿਤੁ ਬਿਧਿ:
Declares the divine Name (naam) to be the supreme ambrosial taste (ras), the life-giving spiritual nectar, and expresses urgent longing: how can one come to taste this highest essence? Presents Naam as the sweetest, most sublime savor and the source of spiritual life, then pleads for the means of access — asking how a human may partake of that restorative, transcendent flavor.

Themes: naam (the Divine Name), ras/ambrosial taste, spiritual nourishment, longing/yearning, seeking attainment, life-giving nectar
ਬਿਖੈ ਬਨੁ ਫੀਕਾ ਤਿਆਗਿ ਰੀ ਸਖੀਏ ਨਾਮੁ ਮਹਾ ਰਸੁ:
Addresses a companion and urges abandoning the "tasteless water" image of corruption and vice and instead drinking the "supreme nectar" of naam (the divine Name). Insists on renouncing joyless, poisoned worldly pleasures and taking up the sweet, life-giving taste of divine remembrance; repeats the choice as leaving empty, flavorless attachment for nourishing, sustaining God‑contact. It admonishes, instructs, and entices.

Themes: renunciation, naam (divine Name), nectar/taste metaphor, maya/worldly corruption, simran (loving remembrance), exhortation, spiritual sustenance
ਕਬੀਰ ਬਿਰਹੁ ਭੁਯੰਗਮੁ ਮਨਿ ਬਸੈ ਮੰਤੁ ਨ ਮਾਨੈ ਕ:
A coiled snake of separation (birah) lives in the mind: an inner, venomous craving for the Divine that cannot be quelled by ritual formulae. The image says fierce love-longing sits like a serpent in consciousness; no mantra or recitation of naam (the Divine Name) tames it. The teeka notes that taking the Guru (spiritual guide) into refuge awakens this piercing longing.

Themes: snake of separation, inner yearning, futility of mantra, naam/recitation, Guru-refuge, emotional turmoil, uncontrollable longing
ਹਰਿ ਬਿਨੁ ਕਿਉ ਜੀਵਾ ਮੇਰੀ ਮਾਈ ॥:
An urgent plea addressed to the mother-image, confessing that life itself fails without the Lord. The speaker states dependence: without Hari—here read as naam (the divine Name)—existence becomes restless and unbearable. The Divine is cast as life-breath and refuge; the voice laments absence, affirms surrender, and insists loving remembrance/simran (remembrance) alone sustains living.

Themes: mother (caregiver/refuge), Divine presence, naam (the divine Name), dependence, longing, simran (loving remembrance), surrender, life-as-breath
ਪ੍ਰਭ ਮਿਲਬੇ ਕਉ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਿ ਮਨਿ ਲਾਗੀ ॥:
A spontaneous loving longing to meet the Beloved has risen within the mind, declaring an inner turn toward God and commitment to spiritual union. The concrete image — meeting the Beloved — signals refuge, surrender and embrace; restated as yearning, desire to unite, and affectionate attachment to the Divine, preet (devotional love). The mind now inclines toward devotion and away from worldly ties.

Themes: meeting the Beloved (image), loving longing/yearning, mind’s turn/inner awakening, surrender/refuge, devotional attachment (preet), union with God, detachment from maya (worldly attachment)
ਹਰਿ ਦਰਸਨ ਕਉ ਮੇਰਾ ਮਨੁ ਬਹੁ ਤਪਤੈ ਜਿਉ ਤ੍ਰਿਖਾ:
The mind aches and burns with urgent, pleading thirst for the Lord’s Blessed Vision (darshan); the concrete image is a thirsty man denied water, and the teeka adds that the wound is from the arrow of divine love, so the soul is pierced and restless. The heart longs, the inner self thirsts, the consciousness is consumed until it beholds the Beloved.

Themes: thirsty imagery, yearning for darshan (Blessed Vision), love’s arrow, burning desire, devotional plea, mind’s torment, longing for union, simran (loving remembrance)
ਬਾਝਹੁ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਕੋਇ ਨ ਸਾਰੇ ਏਕਲੜੀ ਕੁਰਲਾਏ ॥:
Alone in a barren wilderness, the speaker cries out with no one to care except the Beloved — Piare (the Divine). This is a plaintive plea and confession: announcing total abandonment by human ties, exposing solitary suffering, and turning dependence wholly toward God’s compassion. It laments being ignored, declares God the sole refuge, and seeks mercy through heartfelt yearning.

Themes: Beloved (Piare) as refuge, solitude and wilderness image, lament and pleading, abandonment by creation, dependence on Divine compassion, turning to God, yearning for attention.
ਮਨਿ ਬੈਰਾਗੁ ਭਇਆ ਦਰਸਨੁ ਦੇਖਣੈ ਕਾ ਚਾਉ ॥:
Declares an inner conversion: the mind has become bairag (dispassion), freed from maya (worldly attachment) because love for the Divine has been born; the heart now aches to see darshan (vision of God's presence). It affirms detachment as passionate longing rather than cold renunciation — dispassion born of love, thirsting, yearning to behold the Beloved.

Themes: mind, bairag (dispassion), love-born longing, darshan (vision of God), renunciation, devotional yearning, inner transformation
ਘਰਿ ਆਵਹੁ ਚਿਰੀ ਵਿਛੁੰਨਿਆ ਮਿਲੁ ਸਬਦਿ ਗੁਰੂ ਪ੍:
A direct, urgent plea asking God to return and take residence in the speaker’s inner home, confessing a long, painful separation. The devotee begs to be reunited and absorbed into the Divine, insisting that this union happen through the Guru’s Shabad (the divine Word). It calls for God to come dwell in the heart, end exile, and restore intimate, inward communion.

Themes: home as inner dwelling, separation/longing, reunion and merging, Guru’s Shabad (Word), pleading/petition, heart as abode, surrender.
ਪਿਰ ਦੋਸੁ ਨਾਹੀ ਸੁਖਹ ਦਾਤੇ ਹਉ ਵਿਛੁੜੀ ਬੁਰਿਆਰ:
Addresses the Divine as Husband‑Lord and Giver of peace — an image of refuge and surrender — and declares God blameless while admitting separation results from my own evil deeds. Humble self-confession retracts blame, accepts full responsibility, and pleads contritely for reunion; the stance is repentance, inward accounting, longing and surrender.

Themes: Husband‑Lord image, Divine blamelessness, self-responsibility, separation by karma, repentance, longing for union, humility
ਆਉ ਜੀ ਤੂ ਆਉ ਹਮਾਰੈ ਹਰਿ ਜਸੁ ਸ੍ਰਵਨ ਸੁਨਾਵਨਾ:
A pleading to the beloved Guru: come and dwell in the home of my heart so that my ears may hear the Lord’s Praises. The concrete image — the heart as a dwelling and the ears as receptacles of praise — expresses a request for divine indwelling that makes inward hearing of naam (the divine Name) and sustained simran (loving remembrance) possible. Tone: longing, supplicatory, seeking inner transformation.

Themes: heart-as-home, divine indwelling (Guru’s presence), hearing/praise, supplication/longing, naam (the divine Name), simran (loving remembrance), inner transformation, devotion
ਆਉ ਹਮਾਰੈ ਰਾਮ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਜੀਉ ॥:
A direct, intimate plea that begs the Beloved Lord to come and dwell in the speaker’s heart. It invites divine indwelling, seeking closeness, union and refuge through inner residence rather than distant worship. It opens the self in surrender, expressing yearning, devotion and urgent request for God to take up residence and transform the inner life.

Themes: longing, plea, Divine indwelling (dwell in my heart), surrender, devotion (bhakti), union, naam (the divine Name), simran (loving remembrance)
ਬਿਨਵੰਤਿ ਨਾਨਕ ਦਇਆ ਧਾਰਹੁ ਘਰਿ ਆਵਹੁ ਨਾਹ ਪਿਆਰ:
A soul-persona as wife entreats the Beloved Husband (piare pati) to grant daya (mercy) and return to dwell in her heart-home. It is an intimate, pleading invocation: beseeching God to come home, to abide and end the pain of separation, to bring compassionate indwelling and union rather than issuing teaching or judgment.

Themes: mercy (daya), Beloved Husband (piare pati), heart as home, longing, supplication, divine indwelling, conjugal imagery, union
ਮੋਹਨ ਘਰਿ ਆਵਹੁ ਕਰਉ ਜੋਦਰੀਆ ॥:
An intimate plea: the speaker begs the Fascinating Lord (Mohan) to enter and abide in their house—the teeka makes that house the heart—inviting the Divine to take up residence as an inner presence. It is a petition for indwelling and surrender, a longing for intimate union, asking God to make the heart His home through devotion and simran (loving remembrance).

Themes: heart-as-home, indwelling Divine presence, pleading/supplication, surrender, longing for union, simran (loving remembrance)
ਹਮ ਘਰਿ ਸਾਜਨ ਆਏ ॥:
Declares joyful arrival: friends — the Lord as intimate companions — have entered the home of the heart, the concrete image of God manifesting within. Praising and celebrating inner nearness, it proclaims divine companionship and residence rather than distant worship. The inward home is established by simran (loving remembrance) and naam (the Divine Name), making God friend and resident.

Themes: friends (divine companions), home/heart, divine manifestation, simran (loving remembrance), naam (the Divine Name), intimacy, devotional joy
ਪਹਿਲੈ ਪਹਰੈ ਫੁਲੜਾ ਫਲੁ ਭੀ ਪਛਾ ਰਾਤਿ ॥:
Compares two night-watches: the first watch’s devotion is a flower—beautiful, sensory, early-stage practice—while the later watches yield fruit, the lasting reward or amrit (nectar) of realization. Praises and instructs steady bandagi (devotion): initial enthusiasm is attractive but transient; continued, deeper vigil produces real spiritual fruit and maturation of practice.

Themes: night-watches, flower (early beauty), fruit/amrit (lasting reward), bandagi (devotion), perseverance, maturation of practice, reward of sustained worship
ਕਬੀਰ ਸੂਤਾ ਕਿਆ ਕਰਹਿ ਉਠਿ ਕਿ ਨ ਜਪਹਿ ਮੁਰਾਰਿ:
A sharp self-rebuke using the image of sleep: the speaker scolds himself for dozing in maya (worldly attachment), wasting his life as age passes, and failing to rise. It urgently orders waking, rising, and practicing simran (loving remembrance) — meditating on naam (the divine Name). Admonishes heedlessness, presses urgency, and calls for disciplined, vigilant devotion.

Themes: wakefulness, simran (loving remembrance), naam (the divine Name), maya (worldly attachment), urgency/impermanence, self-admonition, vigilance
ਪਰਭਾਤੇ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਿ ਗੁਰ ਕੇ ਚਰਣ ਧਿਆਇ ॥:
Rise in the ambrosial early-morning hour and chant the Naam (the divine Name); meditate on the Guru’s feet as humble reverence and the living gateway to God. It instructs disciplined waking for simran (loving remembrance), continual repetition of God’s Name, and heartfelt surrender to the Guru as refuge and the connector to the Divine — wake, remember, surrender.

Themes: ambrosial hour, naam (divine Name), simran (loving remembrance), Guru’s feet (refuge/surrender), humility, discipline, devotion
ਝਾਲਾਘੇ ਉਠਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਿ ਨਿਸਿ ਬਾਸੁਰ ਆਰਾਧਿ ॥:
Imperative command to rise in amrit vela (the ambrosial pre-dawn hour) and chant the naam (the divine Name), then keep simran (loving remembrance) and worship continuously—day and night. It instructs disciplined sadhana: early waking, repeated Naam recitation, unbroken adoration and devotion as the core purpose of life; the teeka stresses pre-dawn practice plus nonstop remembrance.

Themes: amrit vela, naam (the divine Name), simran (loving remembrance), waking/discipline, continuous devotion, worship/adoration
ਬਾਬੀਹਾ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਵੇਲੈ ਬੋਲਿਆ ਤਾਂ ਦਰਿ ਸੁਣੀ ਪ:
A lone rainbird (papiha) calling in the ambrosial pre-dawn (amrit vela) symbolizes the soul (jeev) waking to cry out; its small, natural song becomes a heartfelt supplication, and that simple plea is received in the Divine Court. The passage urges early, wakeful simran (loving remembrance) and naam (the divine Name), reassuring that humble, instinctive devotion is heard and answered.

Themes: rainbird (papiha) image and soul’s longing, amrit vela (ambrosial pre-dawn) as receptive hour, simran/naam (loving remembrance/the divine Name), prayer heard in the Divine Court, humble supplication, wakeful devotion, divine receptivity
ਛਾਤੀ ਸੀਤਲ ਮਨੁ ਸੁਖੀ ਛੰਤ ਗੋਬਿਦ ਗੁਨ ਗਾਇ ॥:
Singing the Glorious Praises cools the chest and soothes the heart, bringing the mind to peaceful rest; it declares relief and joy through worship. Devotional chanting — naam (the divine Name), simran (loving remembrance) and kirtan — turns inner heat and turmoil into calm, converts agitation to contentment, and presents praise as the remedy and refuge.

Themes: cooled chest (physical image), inner peace, praise/adoration, naam, simran, kirtan (devotional music), solace/comfort, transformation of unrest into calm
ਜੋਗੁ ਬਨਿਆ ਤੇਰਾ ਕੀਰਤਨੁ ਗਾਈ ॥੧॥:
By singing the Kirtan (sacred singing of the Name), the speaker attains Yoga — an inner yogic state, spiritual union and disciplined absorption. Singing God’s praises is both the method and the reward: devotional song produces meditative union, devotional immersion, and grants the double comfort the teeka notes — worldly ease and fakiri (ascetic) peace. It both praises and prescribes kirtan as the path.

Themes: kirtan (sacred singing), yoga (spiritual union), devotional practice, meditative absorption, worldly comfort, fakiri/ascetic peace, praise as means
ਹਉ ਅਨਦਿਨੁ ਹਰਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਕੀਰਤਨੁ ਕਰਉ ॥:
Declares unwavering devotion: night and day the speaker sings kirtan (singing praises) of the naam (the divine Name), practicing simran (loving remembrance) without pause. It praises and affirms a life wholly given to praise, making continuous worship the speaker’s identity and discipline; it models perpetual recitation, constant remembrance, and unceasing praise as the way to live.

Themes: night-and-day constancy, naam (the divine Name), kirtan (singing praises), simran (remembrance), devotion as identity, continuous practice, praise/surrender
ਰੁਣ ਝੁਣੋ ਸਬਦੁ ਅਨਾਹਦੁ ਨਿਤ ਉਠਿ ਗਾਈਐ ਸੰਤਨ ਕ:
Commands waking before dawn and joining the sangat (the company of the devout) to sing the Shabad (the unstruck Divine Word) together; it prescribes a daily, communal discipline of sweet melodic praise that attunes the heart to naam (the Divine Name) through kirtan. Instructs early rising, group singing, continual simran (loving remembrance) — making devotional music the life-practice.

Themes: early rising, sangat, Shabad, kirtan (devotional music), naam, simran, daily discipline, communal devotion
ਸਾਧੋ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਕੇ ਗੁਨ ਗਾਵਉ ॥:
Addressing saadhus (holy devotees), an imperative calling for unceasing praise: sing Gobind’s glorious qualities, keep reciting and celebrating the Lord of the Universe, and make continual glorification and remembrance the steady practice. It urges sustained, vocal devotion—public or private—as the prescribed way to praise, remember, and embody the Divine presence and virtues.

Themes: praise (glorification), saadhus (holy devotees), continual remembrance (simran, loving remembrance), vocal praise/kirtan (devotional singing), divine attributes, exhortation/command, devotion.
ਨਿਰਬਾਣ ਕੀਰਤਨੁ ਗਾਵਹੁ ਕਰਤੇ ਕਾ ਨਿਮਖ ਸਿਮਰਤ ਜ:
Urges the seeker to adopt a desireless, Nirvaanaa-like stance (vasna-rahit) and perform kirtan (devotional singing) of the Creator while practising simran (loving remembrance; naam, the divine Name). It instructs and guarantees: by the Creator’s blessing, even a momentary remembrance, an instant of heartfelt nama-simran, purifies the mind, severs vices and grants liberation.

Themes: Nirvaan (liberation), kirtan (devotional singing), simran/naam (remembrance of the Name), vasna-rahit (desirelessness), instantaneous grace, purification from vices, practical sadhana (practice)
ਮਨ ਮੀਠ ਤੁਹਾਰੋ ਕੀਓ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥:
The speaker declares wholehearted acceptance and praise: the mind (man) finds every act of the Divine sweet — delight, approval, and contentment with God's will. It praises and surrenders rather than questions, accepting all Divine action as pleasing. The Punjabi teeka adds exclusivity: the poet never praises any other for favors, reserving all praise and pleasure for God alone.

Themes: Divine action, mind's delight, acceptance/surrender, praise/exclusivity, contentment, non-judgment, gratitude
ਮੀਤ ਕੇ ਕਰਤਬ ਕੁਸਲ ਸਮਾਨਾ ॥੧॥:
Declares intimate approval and delight in the Friend’s actions, praising the Divine's deeds as comforting and pleasing. The concrete image is the Friend’s actions; the idea beneath is finding solace, trust and surrender in divine will—accepting and delighting in what God does, rejoicing in and approving the Lord’s conduct. It reassures the mind and affirms contentment in God's ways.

Themes: Divine actions, praise and delight, trust/acceptance, solace and comfort, surrender, contentment
ਸਰਬ ਸੁਖ ਆਨੰਦ ਮੰਗਲ ਰਸ ਮਾਨਿ ਗੋਬਿੰਦੈ ਆਗਿਓ ॥:
Surrendering to the Lord of the Universe’s Will (Hukam) brings complete peace, joy, happiness and auspiciousness; it declares that accepting God’s sweet will is the source of all contentment. Acceptance of Divine will produces inner calm and blessedness; yielding ego and resisting no longer opens the heart to every bliss and spiritual fulfillment.

Themes: Hukam (Divine Will), surrender/acceptance, peace/joy, contentment, gratitude, devotion, renunciation
ਖਿਨ ਮਹਿ ਥਾਪਿ ਉਥਾਪਨਹਾਰਾ ਆਪਨ ਹਾਥਿ ਮਤਾਤ ॥੧॥:
Declares God's absolute sovereignty: He sets up and pulls down in an instant, creating and destroying at a breath's notice; He ordains every rise and fall by His will. The concrete image of hands holding all matters says every decision, birth and death, fate and outcome rests in His grasp, urging surrender and recognition of human transience.

Themes: Divine sovereignty, creation and dissolution, transience of life, divine will, fate, surrender, human powerlessness
ਨਾਨਕ ਨਾਮੁ ਧਿਆਈਐ ਕਾਰਜੁ ਆਵੈ ਰਾਸਿ ॥੧॥:
Meditating on the Naam (the divine Name) anchors the mind in simran (loving remembrance) and draws life into God’s presence; as a result, one’s affairs, tasks and troubles are set right. The tone is direct instruction and promise: persistent remembrance centers action, aligns outcomes with divine will, and secures practical resolution and grace.

Themes: naam (the divine Name), simran (loving remembrance), divine grace, providence, practical resolution, surrender, spiritual practice
ਕਾਰਜੁ ਤੇਰਾ ਹੋਵੈ ਪੂਰਾ ਹਰਿ ਹਰਿ ਹਰਿ ਗੁਣ ਗਾਇ:
Addresses the mind directly: O my mind, sing the Glorious Praises—Har, Har, Har—and trust that your affairs will be perfectly accomplished. It instructs simran (loving remembrance) and chanting the Name, naam (the divine Name), as active devotion; praise functions as both command and promise, the practice by which work is completed and bears fruit.

Themes: naam, simran, praise, assurance of success, inner admonition, fulfilled action, devotional practice
ਨਾਨਕ ਨਾਮੁ ਅਰਾਧਣਾ ਕਾਰਜੁ ਆਵੈ ਰਾਸਿ ॥੮॥:
Commands the seeker to fix the mind on naam (the divine Name) by simran (loving remembrance), promising that dwelling in the Name settles all affairs: worldly tasks succeed, inner longings are fulfilled, obstacles vanish. It both praises and instructs—worship and constant remembrance are the practical means; the blessing of simran brings completion and the fulfilment of life’s purpose.

Themes: naam (the divine Name), simran (loving remembrance), devotion/worship, resolved affairs, fulfilment of life-purpose, divine blessing, instruction/command, removal of obstacles
ਸਭੇ ਕਾਜ ਸਵਾਰਿਐ ਜਾ ਤੁਧੁ ਭਾਵੰਦਾ ॥੭॥:
When the Lord’s pleasure (raza) is granted, my affairs are put in order; my tasks are resolved and life’s projects fall into place. It declares cause and effect: Divine favor produces concrete results. It praises grace, affirms reliance on God rather than self-effort, and expresses calm confidence and thankful surrender in the face of worldly concerns.

Themes: raza (Divine pleasure), grace as cause, worldly affairs resolved, reliance on God, surrender, thanksgiving, peace
ਸਗਲ ਮਨੋਰਥ ਪੂਰਨ ਹੋਏ ਕਦੇ ਨ ਹੋਇ ਦੁਖਾਲਾ ਜੀਉ:
Declares a final, complete satisfaction: every hope, want and need is fulfilled, and the heart is assured it will never again suffer sorrow. Praises the settled peace of fulfilled longing—desires met, needs satisfied, grief removed—portraying concrete wishes become spiritual contentment and permanent release from pain. Stance is confident proclamation and celebration of enduring deliverance.

Themes: fulfilled desires, contentment, freedom from sorrow, permanence, release/liberation, assurance, satisfied longings
